title: Grammatical Gender & Adjective-Noun Agreement
subtitle: Determine noun gender by its ending and match the modifying adjective.
keyPoint: In the nominative case, Polish adjectives must agree in gender with the noun they describe, usually ending in -y/-i for masculine, -a for feminine, and -e for neuter.

useCases.label: Masculine nouns
useCases.example: Ten stary stół stoi w pokoju.

examples.en: To czyste miasto ma piękny park.
Polski język bywa trudny dla obcokrajowców.

mistakes.note: Kawa ends in -a and is feminine, so the adjective must take the feminine ending -a.
Telefon ends in a consonant and is masculine, so it requires the masculine adjective ending -y.
Okno ends in -o and is neuter, requiring the neuter adjective ending -e.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'a good tea' (herbata is feminine):
quiz.explanation: Herbata is feminine singular, so the adjective must end in -a (dobra).

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'a big car' (samochód is masculine):
quiz.explanation: Samochód is masculine singular ending in a consonant, taking the masculine ending -y (duży).

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'a modern apartment' (mieszkanie is neuter):
quiz.explanation: Mieszkanie ends in -e and is neuter, so the adjective must take the neuter suffix -e (nowoczesne).

quiz.question: Which noun correctly matches the masculine adjective 'drogi' (expensive)?
quiz.explanation: Zegarek ends in a consonant and is masculine, matching the masculine adjective drogi.

tip: Look at the very last letter of a noun: a consonant usually signals masculine, -a signals feminine, and -o/-e/-ę signal neuter.

title: Present Tense Conjugation Groups
subtitle: Master the personal endings of Polish present tense verbs.
keyPoint: Polish verbs fall into three major present-tense groups defined by their 1st and 2nd person singular endings: -am/-asz, -ę/-isz (or -ysz), and -ę/-esz.

examples.en: Mieszkam w Warszawie od dwóch lat.
Studenci piszą trudny egzamin z gramatyki.

mistakes.note: Verbs must be conjugated for person; do not leave verbs in the infinitive (-ć).
The second person singular (ty) of robić requires the ending -isz: robisz.
Group 1 verbs take -ają in the third person plural (oni/one), not the singular form -a.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ja ___ po polsku.' (rozmawiać - Group 1)
quiz.explanation: For ja (I) in Group 1 verbs, add -am to the stem: rozmawiam.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Czy ty ___ kawę?' (pić - Group 3)
quiz.explanation: The second-person singular (ty) ending for Group 3 is -esz: pijesz.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Mój brat ___ w Krakowie.' (mieszkać - Group 1)
quiz.explanation: Third-person singular (on/ona/ono) in Group 1 takes -a: mieszka.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Oni ___ zadanie domowe.' (robić - Group 2)
quiz.explanation: The third-person plural (oni) in Group 2 takes -ą: robią.

tip: Subject pronouns like ja (I) and ty (you) are normally omitted in Polish because the verb suffix already makes the subject crystal clear.

title: Instrumental Case for Identity and Profession
subtitle: State professions, nationalities, and roles with the verb 'być'.
keyPoint: When describing a person's profession, role, or nationality with the verb 'być' (to be), Polish requires both the noun and adjective to be in the instrumental case.

mistakes.note: With the verb 'być', a predicate noun designating a status must be in the instrumental case (-em).
Feminine nouns in the instrumental case take the nasal vowel ending -ą.
Both the adjective AND the noun must decline together into the instrumental case.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Adam jest świetnym ___.' (programista - masculine)
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns ending in -a decline like feminine nouns in the instrumental, taking -ą (programistą).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Katarzyna jest miłą ___.' (dziewczyna - feminine)
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns take the instrumental singular ending -ą (dziewczyną).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Mój brat jest ___ kucharzem.' (dobry - masculine adjective)
quiz.explanation: Masculine adjectives take -ym (or -im after k/g) in the instrumental singular: dobrym.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Magda jest znaną ___.' (aktorka - feminine)
quiz.explanation: The feminine instrumental ending is -ą, yielding aktorką.

tip: Remember the shortcut: masculine instrumental ends in -em (noun) and -ym/-im (adjective), while feminine instrumental ends in -ą for BOTH noun and adjective.

title: Accusative Case & Animacy
subtitle: Form direct objects and distinguish masculine living things from objects.
keyPoint: Direct objects take the accusative case; inanimate masculine nouns look identical to the nominative, whereas animate masculine nouns take the genitive-like ending -a.

useCases.label: Masculine animate object
useCases.example: Widzę twojego czarnego kota w ogrodzie.

examples.en: On ma małego psa i rudego kota.

mistakes.note: Feminine direct objects change from -a to -ę for the noun and -a to -ą for the adjective.
Inanimate masculine objects remain unchanged in the accusative (identical to the nominative).
Brat is a person (animate), so the accusative takes genitive endings: tego brata.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Czytam ciekawą ___.' (książka - feminine)
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular nouns change from -a to -ę in the accusative case (książkę).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Kupuję nowy ___.' (telefon - masculine inanimate)
quiz.explanation: Inanimate masculine nouns keep their nominative form in the accusative case (telefon).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Widzę twojego ___.' (pies - masculine animate)
quiz.explanation: Animate masculine nouns take the ending -a (with a stem shift for pies -> psa).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ona ma ___ zupę.' (smaczna - feminine adjective)
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular adjectives take the nasal vowel ending -ą in the accusative case (smaczną).

tip: Neuter nouns and masculine inanimate things never change in the accusative—they look exactly like their dictionary (nominative) forms.

title: Genitive of Negation
subtitle: Transform accusative direct objects into the genitive when negating verbs.
keyPoint: Whenever a transitive verb that governs the accusative case is negated with 'nie', the direct object MUST switch to the genitive case.

useCases.label: Negating masculine objects
useCases.example: Mam ten telefon, ale nie mam tego telefonu.

useCases.label: Negating feminine objects
useCases.example: Lubię tę kawę, ale nie lubię tej kawy.

useCases.label: Negating neuter objects
useCases.example: Znam to słowo, ale nie pamiętam tego słowa.

examples.en: Anna nie lubi mleka w kawie.

mistakes.note: Negating the verb 'mieć' triggers the genitive of negation; accusative 'czas' must become 'czasu'.
Under negation, feminine accusative (-ą / -ę) shifts to genitive (-ej / -y).
Masculine nouns and demonstratives must shift to genitive endings (-ego / -a) under negation.

quiz.question: Complete the negated sentence: 'Mam ochotę, ale on nie ma ___.' (ochota - feminine)
quiz.explanation: The feminine genitive singular takes the ending -y (ochoty) after a negated verb.

quiz.question: Complete the negated sentence: 'Kupuję chleb, ale nie kupuję ___.' (ser - masculine)
quiz.explanation: In the genitive of negation, masculine food items typically take the -a ending (sera).

quiz.question: Complete the negated sentence: 'Nie znam ___ pana.' (ten nowy - masculine)
quiz.explanation: Masculine adjectives and demonstratives take -ego in the genitive case (tego nowego).

quiz.question: Complete the negated sentence: 'Dziecko nie pije ___.' (mleko - neuter)
quiz.explanation: Neuter nouns take the genitive singular ending -a (mleka).

tip: Think of 'nie' as an automatic switch: whenever 'nie' appears right before a transitive verb, swap the direct object into the genitive case immediately.

title: Locative Case with Static Prepositions
subtitle: Talking about static locations and topics using w, na, o, and przy
keyPoint: The locative case is exclusively governed by prepositions like 'w', 'na', 'o', 'przy', and causes hard stem consonants to soften or mutate before endings like -e or -u.

cells: Soft stem or velar (k, g, ch) -> -u

useCases.label: On an open surface or event (na)

mistakes.note: Preposition 'w' demands the locative case, mutating 'k' to 'c' with the ending '-e'.
Neuter nouns ending in '-o' take '-e' in the locative, softening 'n' to 'ni'.
Static location with 'na' requires the locative case with stem vowel alternation (ó -> o).

quiz.question: Adam works in an office (biuro). -> Adam pracuje w ___.
quiz.explanation: Neuter noun 'biuro' takes '-e' in the locative, triggering the mutation 'r' -> 'rz'.

quiz.question: We are talking about Poland (Polska). -> Rozmawiamy o ___.
quiz.explanation: The feminine noun 'Polska' mutates stem 'k' to 'c' and takes '-e'.

quiz.question: The computer is on the table (stół). -> Komputer stoi na ___.
quiz.explanation: The noun 'stół' changes its stem vowel 'ó' to 'o' and takes '-e' ('stole').

quiz.question: My friends are waiting in the park (park). -> Moi znajomi czekają w ___.
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns ending in velar consonants like 'k' take the '-u' ending in the locative.

tip: Remember: The locative case is never used alone without a preposition; look out for 'w', 'na', 'o', 'przy', and 'po'.

title: Verbal Aspect: Imperfective vs. Perfective
subtitle: Distinguishing continuous processes and habits from completed results
keyPoint: Polish verbs come in pairs: imperfective expresses ongoing processes or habits, while perfective denotes single, completed actions with a clear result.

examples.en: Wczoraj pisałem raport przez trzy godziny.
Napisałem raport i wysłałem go szefowi.
Szybko wypiłem herbatę i wyszedłem z domu.
Ona kupiła nowe mieszkanie w centrum.

mistakes.wrong: Wczoraj przeczytałem książkę przez dwie godziny.
mistakes.right: Wczoraj czytałem książkę przez dwie godziny.
mistakes.note: Durational expressions with 'przez' indicate an ongoing process, requiring the imperfective verb 'czytać'.
Do not mix 'będę' with a perfective infinitive; perfective verbs express the future using simple conjugated forms.
Habitual everyday actions require the imperfective form 'pić'.

quiz.question: Yesterday I was reading all evening, but I didn't finish. -> Wczoraj cały wieczór ___ książkę.
quiz.explanation: The imperfective 'czytałem' highlights the continuous duration rather than the completed result.

quiz.question: I have already finished writing the email. -> Już ___ ten e-mail.
quiz.explanation: The perfective verb 'napisałem' conveys a completed action with a concrete outcome.

quiz.question: Every day Anna buys fresh bread. -> Anna codziennie ___ świeży chleb.
quiz.explanation: Repeated everyday actions use the imperfective present tense 'kupuje'.

quiz.question: Can you open the window? (completed action) -> Czy możesz ___ okno?
quiz.explanation: The perfective infinitive 'otworzyć' expresses completing the specific action once.

tip: Perfective verbs do NOT have a present tense; conjugating a perfective verb immediately creates a future meaning!

title: Past Tense Formation and Gender Agreement
subtitle: Building past actions with the -ł- stem and matching personal endings
keyPoint: Polish past-tense verbs consist of the infinitive stem plus the letter 'ł', followed by distinctive suffixes that explicitly agree with the subject's grammatical gender and number.

useCases.label: Female speaker describing their past
useCases.example: Wczoraj byłam w kinie z siostrą.

useCases.label: Plural group containing at least one man

mistakes.note: A female speaker must use the feminine ending '-łam' instead of the masculine '-łem'.
The noun 'dziecko' is neuter, so the verb requires the neuter past ending '-ło'.

mistakes.wrong: Marek i Ewa poszły do kina.
mistakes.right: Marek i Ewa poszli do kina.
mistakes.note: Any mixed-gender or male plural subject requires the virile (męskoosobowy) past ending '-li'.

quiz.question: A woman says: 'Yesterday I worked late.' -> Wczoraj ___ do późna.
quiz.explanation: A female first-person subject uses the ending '-łam' (pracowałam).

quiz.question: The boy fell asleep quickly. -> Chłopiec szybko ___.
quiz.explanation: A masculine singular 3rd person subject takes the bare '-ł' ending (zasnął).

quiz.question: The girls (non-virile plural) sang beautifully. -> Dziewczyny pięknie ___.
quiz.explanation: All-female or non-virile plural groups take the '-ły' ending in the past tense.

quiz.question: Tom and Mark were at university. -> Tomasz i Marek ___ na uniwersytecie.
quiz.explanation: A masculine personal subject in the plural requires the virile ending '-li' (byli).

tip: Notice how the letter 'ł' softens to 'l' before 'i' in virile plural forms: 'mieli', 'byli', 'robili'.

title: Future Tense: Compound vs. Simple
subtitle: Choosing between future forms of imperfective and perfective verbs
keyPoint: Imperfective future is compound (future 'być' + infinitive or 3rd-person past form), whereas perfective future is simple, formed by conjugating the perfective verb directly.

useCases.label: Planned continuous process (compound)
useCases.example: Jutro będę pracować od rana do nocy.

useCases.label: Single completed future task (simple)
useCases.example: Jutro na pewno skończę ten projekt.

examples.en: Jutro będę gotować obiad dla przyjaciół.
Ona będzie czytała książkę przez całe popołudnie.
Zaraz wypiję kawę i zadzwonię do mamy.
Będziemy studiować język polski w Krakowie.

mistakes.note: Never combine 'będę' with a perfective verb; use the simple perfective form 'napiszę'.
'Zjeść' is perfective, so its future form is the simple conjugated form 'zjem'.

mistakes.wrong: Oni będą robili zakupy, a potem kupią chleb.
mistakes.right: Oni będą robić zakupy, a potem kupią chleb.
mistakes.note: While 'będą robili' is valid, mixing imperfective compound with simple perfective correctly requires keeping aspectual boundaries clear.

quiz.question: Tomorrow I will be learning (ongoing) Polish all day. -> Jutro cały dzień ___ języka polskiego.
quiz.explanation: An ongoing all-day action requires the compound imperfective future 'będę się uczyć'.

quiz.question: I will buy (completed action) this phone tomorrow. -> Jutro ___ ten telefon.
quiz.explanation: Completing the purchase is expressed by the simple perfective future 'kupię'.

quiz.question: What will you be doing this evening? (to a woman) -> Co ___ dzisiaj wieczorem?
quiz.explanation: Compound future with past-participle agreeing with a woman is 'będziesz robiła'.

quiz.question: We will write (finish writing) the test soon. -> Wkrótce ___ ten test.
quiz.explanation: The perfective verb 'napisać' forms the future simply as 'napiszemy'.

tip: Native speakers favor 'będę' + the 3rd person past form (e.g. 'będę czytał/czytała') because it naturally indicates the speaker's gender!

title: Dative Case for Indirect Objects and Impersonal States
subtitle: Giving, helping, and expressing physical or psychological states
keyPoint: The dative case marks the recipient or beneficiary of an action and is used in common impersonal state formulas like 'jest mi zimno'.

examples.en: Czy jest ci ciepło w tym pokoju?

mistakes.note: The verb 'pomagać' requires the dative case ('bratu'), never the accusative or genitive.
Physical sensations use impersonal dative pronouns ('mi'), not nominative subject pronouns ('ja').
The verb 'dziękować' governs the dative ('ci'), not the genitive or accusative.

quiz.question: I am cold. -> Jest ___ bardzo zimno.
quiz.explanation: The short clitic dative pronoun 'mi' is standard for impersonal physical states.

quiz.question: Adam bought flowers for his sister (siostra). -> Adam kupił kwiaty swojej ___.
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns with stem 'r' mutate to 'rz' and take the ending '-e' in the dative case (siostrze).

quiz.question: Can you help the doctor (lekarz)? -> Czy możesz pomóc ___?
quiz.explanation: Most masculine nouns take the ending '-owi' in the dative case (lekarzowi).

quiz.question: We help our parents (rodzice) every weekend. -> Pomagamy naszym ___ w każdy weekend.
quiz.explanation: All plural nouns take the ending '-om' in the dative case.

tip: A tiny group of everyday masculine nouns take '-u' instead of '-owi' in the dative: 'bratu', 'ojcu', 'psu', 'kotu', and 'Bogu'.

title: Imperative Mood and Polite Requests
subtitle: Forming direct commands and softening them with 'proszę'
keyPoint: Direct commands derive from the 3rd person plural present stem, while polite requests use 'proszę' combined with an infinitive.

mistakes.note: Use the infinitive after 'proszę' for polite requests, not the imperative stem.
Use 'proszę + infinitive' (or 'niech Pan zamknie') for formal address, not the informal plural '-cie'.
Use an explicit imperative form rather than an indicative present verb for direct orders.

quiz.question: Tom, ___ okno, proszę! (informal command to one person)
quiz.explanation: Addressing a friend (ty) directly uses the basic singular imperative form 'otwórz'.

quiz.question: Dzieci, ___ natychmiast do pokoju!
quiz.explanation: Addressing a group informally (wy) requires adding the '-cie' suffix to the stem: 'idźcie'.

quiz.question: Szanowni Państwo, ___ chwilę poczekać.
quiz.explanation: The fixed formula for polite requests directed to adults uses the 1st person singular 'proszę' followed by an infinitive.

quiz.question: Jest późno, ___ już do domu! (Let's...)
quiz.explanation: First-person plural imperatives (let's) take the ending '-my': 'wracajmy'.

tip: For negative commands with 'nie', Polish overwhelmingly prefers the imperfective aspect (e.g., 'Nie rób tego!', not 'Nie zrób tego!').

title: Verbs of Motion: Determinate vs. Indeterminate
subtitle: Choosing between unidirectional and multidirectional or habitual movements
keyPoint: Determinate verbs describe motion in one direction right now, while indeterminate verbs describe round trips, repeated trips, or general abilities.

cells: Going in one specific direction right now
Wandering, pacing, round trips, or general ability

useCases.label: Currently Underway
useCases.example: Teraz idę do sklepu po chleb.

examples.en: On często chodzi na długie spacery.

mistakes.note: Use indeterminate 'chodzić' for habitual, repeated actions accompanied by 'codziennie'.

mistakes.wrong: Teraz chodzę na dworzec, bo mam pociąg.
mistakes.right: Teraz idę na dworzec, bo mam pociąg.
mistakes.note: Use determinate 'iść' for an action currently unfolding in one specific direction.
General physical ability or recreational movement requires the indeterminate verb 'jeździć'.

quiz.question: Cześć Kasia! Gdzie teraz ___?
quiz.explanation: The speaker asks about a specific movement happening right now ('teraz'), demanding the determinate verb 'iść' (2nd person: 'idziesz').

quiz.question: Mój brat codziennie ___ tramwajem do szkoły.
quiz.explanation: Habitual transportation requires the indeterminate vehicular verb 'jeździć' in the 3rd person: 'jeździ'.

quiz.question: W każdą sobotę ___ na basen.
quiz.explanation: 'W każdą sobotę' indicates a weekly routine, demanding the indeterminate verb 'chodzimy'.

quiz.question: Uważaj na drodze! Bardzo szybko ___!
quiz.explanation: A direct comment on current unidirectional vehicular motion requires 'jechać' (2nd person: 'jedziesz').

tip: Think of 'iść/jechać' as a single arrow pointing forward (→), and 'chodzić/jeździć' as repeated loops or back-and-forth arrows (⇄).

title: Virile vs. Non-Virile Plural Forms
subtitle: Distinguishing męskoosobowy from niemęskoosobowy agreement
keyPoint: Polish divides all plural forms into virile (groups containing at least one male human) and non-virile (all other people, animals, and things).

useCases.label: Male/Mixed Human Groups
useCases.example: Moi koledzy byli wczoraj w kinie.

useCases.label: Inanimate / Animal Plural
useCases.example: Te nowe samochody stały na parkingu.

examples.en: One kupiły świeże owoce na targu.

mistakes.wrong: Moi koledzy były wczoraj w kawiarni.
mistakes.right: Moi koledzy byli wczoraj w kawiarni.
mistakes.note: Groups of men or mixed genders take the virile past ending '-li', never '-ły'.

mistakes.wrong: Te mądre panowie rozmawiali o polityce.
mistakes.right: Ci mądrzy panowie rozmawiali o polityce.
mistakes.note: Virile nouns require virile demonstratives ('ci') and adjectives ('mądrzy'), not non-virile forms ('te', 'mądre').

mistakes.wrong: Kobiety i dzieci byli w parku.
mistakes.right: Kobiety i dzieci były w parku.
mistakes.note: If a group contains women and children but no adult males, it remains grammatically non-virile ('były').

quiz.question: Nowi pracownicy ___ spóźnieni do biura.
quiz.explanation: 'Pracownicy' is virile (męskoosobowy), so the past tense plural verb requires the '-li' ending: 'byli'.

quiz.question: ___ dziewczyny czytały interesującą książkę.
quiz.explanation: 'Dziewczyny' is non-virile (all female), which demands the non-virile demonstrative and adjective: 'Te mądre'.

quiz.question: Marek i Anna ___ wczoraj długo w nocy.
quiz.explanation: A mixed group of at least one male human and any female/inanimate companions behaves as virile: 'rozmawiali'.

quiz.question: Wszystkie moje koty ___ smaczne jedzenie.
quiz.explanation: Animals are always grammatically non-virile in the plural, taking the '-ły' ending: 'zjadły'.

tip: Even a group of ninety-nine women and one man triggers the virile forms: 'oni byli', 'nasi znajomi'.

title: Numeral Syntax and Noun Governance
subtitle: Contrasting numbers 2–4 with 5 and higher in subject positions
keyPoint: Subject numbers 2–4 take Nominative plural nouns and plural verbs, whereas numbers 5 and up govern Genitive plural nouns and neuter singular verbs.

examples.en: Dwa duże psy biegały w ogrodzie.
Sześć małych dzieci bawiło się w parku.
Trzy nowe okna kosztowały dużo pieniędzy.

mistakes.note: Numerals from 5 upward govern the Genitive plural ('studentek') and a 3rd person neuter singular verb ('zdało').
Numbers 2, 3, and 4 (ending without virile syntax) take Nominative plural ('koty') and plural verbs ('spały').
Subject constructions governed by numerals 5+ require neuter singular past verbs ending in '-ło'.

quiz.question: Na parkingu stoją ___ nowe samochody.
quiz.explanation: The noun 'samochody' and verb 'stoją' are in the Nominative plural, which pairs with 'trzy' (2-4 pattern).

quiz.question: W klasie było ___ utalentowanych uczniów.
quiz.explanation: The Genitive plural 'uczniów' combined with the neuter singular verb 'było' requires a numeral of 5 or higher: 'piętnaście'.

quiz.question: Cztery nowe koleżanki ___ do naszej grupy.
quiz.explanation: Non-virile plural subject 'cztery koleżanki' requires regular plural feminine verb agreement: 'dołączyły'.

quiz.question: Osiem dziewcząt ___ wczoraj do muzeum.
quiz.explanation: Numerals 5 and up take neuter singular verb agreement in the past tense: 'poszło'.

tip: Check the last word of compound numbers: 22, 33, 44 trigger the 2–4 rule (Nominative plural), but 25, 36, 48 trigger the 5+ rule (Genitive plural).

title: Conditional Mood and Movable Particles
subtitle: Forming counterfactual statements with the flexible particle '-by-'
keyPoint: The conditional particle '-by-' adds personal endings (-m, -ś, -, -śmy, -ście) and can attach directly to the past-tense verb stem or jump to conjunctions.

useCases.label: Hypothetical Condition
useCases.example: Gdybym miał czas, poszedłbym do kina.

examples.en: Gdybyś uczyła się regularnie, zdałabyś ten test.
Gdybyśmy mieli pieniądze, pojechalibyśmy do Włoch.

mistakes.wrong: Gdybym ja miał czas, to ja kupiłbym to.
mistakes.right: Gdybym miał czas, to kupiłbym to.
mistakes.note: Avoid doubling pronouns unnecessarily; the personal markers '-m' already specify the subject.
Keep clitic pronouns un-stressed ('ci', not 'tobie') unless placed deliberately at sentence beginnings or under contrastive emphasis.
Attach the second-person conditional ending to the subordinating conjunction ('żebyś'), not leaving the verb stranded without proper agreement.

quiz.question: Gdybym ___ więcej wolnego czasu, czytałbym książki.
quiz.explanation: The conditional marker '-m' has attached to 'gdyby' ('gdybym'), so the following verb appears in the plain past-tense base without personal suffix: 'miał'.

quiz.question: Czy ___ mi pomóc z tą walizką? (speaking to an informal male friend)
quiz.explanation: Addressing an informal male peer (ty) in the conditional requires the masculine stem + '-byś': 'mógłbyś'.

quiz.question: Chętnie ___ do teatru w ten weekend. (we, mixed group)
quiz.explanation: A virile 1st-person plural subject ('we') requires '-libyśmy': 'poszlibyśmy'.

quiz.question: Mama prosiła, ___ natychmiast wrócili do domu. (you plural)
quiz.explanation: When directing the clause to 'wy' (2nd person plural), attach '-ście' to 'żeby': 'żebyście'.

tip: Polish conditional personal endings are mobile clitics: 'My byśmy to zrobili' and 'Zrobilibyśmy to' mean the exact same thing.

title: Functions of 'Się': Reflexive, Reciprocal, and Impersonal
subtitle: Master the versatile roles of the clitic 'się' in Polish syntax.
keyPoint: The particle 'się' signals whether the subject acts upon itself, interacts reciprocally with another entity, or creates a generalized impersonal statement.

cells: Subject and direct object are identical (oneself)
Mutual action between multiple subjects (each other)
Subjectless general statement (one does / it is done)
Lexical requirement; verb does not exist without 'się'

useCases.label: Self-Directed Action
useCases.example: Dziecko ubiera się samodzielnie przed wyjściem.

useCases.label: Mutual Interaction
useCases.example: Często spotykamy się w kawiarni w centrum miasta.

useCases.label: General Rule / Impersonal
useCases.example: Jak to słowo wymawia się poprawnie?

examples.en: Codziennie czeszę się przed wielkim lustrem.
Oni bardzo się lubią i wspólnie pracują.
W tej restauracji podaje się tradycyjne potrawy.
Boję się ciemności w tym starym domu.
Wszyscy serdecznie się przywitali na lotnisku.

mistakes.note: Never use the personal accusative pronoun ('mnie', 'cię') for self-directed actions; Polish requires the reflexive particle 'się'.
Avoid placing 'się' as the very first element of a sentence; it is a clitic that prefers a post-verbal or unstressed mid-sentence slot.
Polish expresses reciprocity ('each other') naturally with 'się' rather than calquing analytical phrases.

quiz.question: How do you say 'They help each other regularly' in natural Polish?
quiz.explanation: Verbs requiring the dative case (like 'pomagać') take the dative reflexive pronoun 'sobie' rather than accusative 'się' for reciprocity.

quiz.question: Select the impersonal construction meaning 'One speaks Polish here':
quiz.explanation: The 3rd-person singular verb followed by 'się' forms standard impersonal expressions.

quiz.question: Choose the correctly constructed sentence for 'The children are dressing themselves':
quiz.explanation: The verb must agree in the 3rd person plural ('ubierają') and use reflexive 'się'.

quiz.question: Which sentence demonstrates an inherent reflexive verb (reflexiva tantum)?
options: W gazecie pisze się o kryzysie.
quiz.explanation: 'Bać się' (to fear) is an inherently reflexive verb; it cannot exist grammatically without 'się'.

tip: Polish rhythmic rhythm disfavors putting 'się' either at the very beginning or the very end of an utterance; aim to tuck it right after the verb or after the first stressed word.

title: Spatial Prefixes on Verbs of Motion
subtitle: Encode trajectory, boundary crossing, and aspect onto motion roots.
keyPoint: Attaching spatial prefixes to determinate motion verbs creates perfective verbs indicating a single, directed movement with specific orientation.

useCases.label: Leaving an Enclosed Space
useCases.example: Marek wyszedł z biura dokładnie o piątej.

useCases.label: Approaching a Boundary
useCases.example: Kiedy dojdziesz do skrzyżowania, skręć w prawo.

useCases.label: Passing Through or Crossing
useCases.example: Pies bezpiecznie przeszedł przez ruchliwą ulicę.

examples.en: Pociąg właśnie odjechał z drugiego peronu.
O której godzinie przyjedziecie do Krakowa?
Musimy obejść to duże jezioro dookoła.
Turyści zeszli ze szczytu przed burzą.

mistakes.note: Use the prefix 'w-' with preposition 'do' for entering, whereas 'wy-' means departing from a space.

mistakes.wrong: On przyjechał z Warszawy do Gdańska na rowerze codziennie.
mistakes.right: On przyjeżdżał z Warszawy do Gdańska na rowerze codziennie.
mistakes.note: Prefixing determinate 'jechać' creates perfective 'przyjechać' (one-off event); use imperfective 'przyjeżdżać' for repeated routines.
'Przejść' means to cross or transit; use 'przyjść' to denote arrival at one's home.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb for 'She left (walked out of) the cinema':
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'wy-' specifies outward motion and matches the preposition 'z' (+ genitive).

quiz.question: How do you say 'We drove across the bridge'?
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'prze-' denotes motion across or through an obstacle, matching 'przez' (+ accusative).

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Pociąg zaraz ___ na stację' (The train will arrive at the station soon):
quiz.explanation: 'Przyjechać' (vehicular arrival) matches arrival at a destination indicated by 'na'.

quiz.question: Which prefix means moving away from a starting point (departure)?
quiz.explanation: The prefix 'od-' encodes departure or distancing from a reference point (e.g., 'odjechać', 'odejść').

tip: Spatial prefixes almost always match paired prepositions: 'w-' takes 'do', 'wy-' takes 'z', 'do-' takes 'do', and 'od-' takes 'od'.

title: Active and Passive Adjectival Participles
subtitle: Form and decline descriptive verbal adjectives in -ący, -ny, and -ty.
keyPoint: Adjectival participles function syntactically like ordinary adjectives, agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun they modify.

useCases.label: Active Ongoing Modifier
useCases.example: Mężczyzna stojący na przystanku czyta gazetę.

useCases.label: Completed State (Passive)
useCases.example: Wszystkie podpisane dokumenty leżą na biurku.

useCases.label: Resultative Condition
useCases.example: Drzwi do gabinetu były szczelnie zamknięte.

examples.en: Pies śpiący na dywanie głośno chrapie.
Pokoje są regularnie sprzątane przez personel.

mistakes.note: Adjectival participles decline: an animate masculine noun in the accusative requires the ending '-ego'.
The agent in a passive participial construction is expressed with 'przez' + accusative, not the instrumental case.
Neuter nouns like 'zadanie' require the neuter participial ending '-e', not feminine '-a'.

quiz.question: Identify the correct participle form: 'Kobieta ___ w pierwszym rzędzie to profesorka' (The woman sitting in the first row):
quiz.explanation: 'Kobieta' is nominative feminine singular, so the active participle must take '-ąca'.

quiz.question: Complete the passive sentence: 'Rachunki zostały już ___' (The bills have already been paid [rachunki = non-virile pl.]):
quiz.explanation: Non-virile plural nouns ('rachunki') take the passive participial ending '-e'.

quiz.question: Choose the correctly formed passive participle for the verb 'otworzyć' (to open):
quiz.explanation: Verbs ending in '-orzyć' take the '-ty' suffix in the passive participle ('otwarty').

quiz.question: Select the correct case agreement: 'Rozmawialiśmy o ___ problemach' (about existing problems - Locative pl.):
quiz.explanation: The locative plural for adjectival endings across all genders is '-ych' / '-ich'.

tip: Active participles (-ący) can only ever be formed from imperfective verbs; perfective active participles do not exist in modern Polish.

title: Contemporaneous and Anterior Adverbial Participles
subtitle: Link simultaneous and sequential clauses with -ąc and -wszy/-łszy.
keyPoint: Adverbial participles are invariable verbal forms that compress subordinate clauses, strictly requiring both actions to share the identical grammatical subject.

useCases.label: Simultaneous Action
useCases.example: Słuchał muzyki, pracując nad nowym projektem.

useCases.label: Preceding Sequence
useCases.example: Zjadłszy obiad, natychmiast wyszedł z domu.

examples.en: Idąc przez park, spotkałem dawnego przyjaciela.
Odpoczywając nad morzem, zapomniał o stresie.
Wszedłszy do pokoju, włączył jasne światło.
Nie wiedząc co powiedzieć, zamilkła na chwilę.

mistakes.right: Kiedy szedłem do szkoły, spadł deszcz.
mistakes.note: Dangling participle: the rain ('deszcz') was not walking to school. Both clauses must have the same subject.
The suffix '-ąc' is exclusive to imperfective verbs; prior completed actions from perfective verbs take '-wszy/-łszy'.
Do not insert redundant subject pronouns directly next to adverbial participles when the main subject follows.

quiz.question: Fill the blank for simultaneous action: 'Rozmawiali, ___ kawę w kawiarni' (drinking coffee):
quiz.explanation: The imperfective contemporaneity marker is the adverbial participle in '-ąc' ('pijąc').

quiz.question: Which sentence demonstrates a grammatically incorrect subject mismatch (dangling participle)?
options: Otworzywszy okno, powiew wiatru przewrócił wazon.
quiz.explanation: In option A, the wind ('powiew') is the grammatical subject, but it didn't open the window.

quiz.question: Form the anterior adverbial participle of the perfective verb 'napisać':
quiz.explanation: Vowel stems take '-wszy': 'napisa-' + '-wszy' = 'napisawszy' (having written).

quiz.question: What is the key functional difference between -ąc and -wszy?
options: -ąc is simultaneous; -wszy indicates an action completed before the main verb.
-ąc is used with nouns; -wszy with adjectives.
-ąc denotes past actions; -wszy denotes future actions.
quiz.explanation: The contemporary participle (-ąc) marks overlapping actions, while the anterior participle (-wszy) marks preceding actions.

tip: Anterior participles (-wszy/-łszy) sound elevated and literary in modern Polish; in casual conversation, native speakers prefer coordinating clauses with 'kiedy' or 'po tym, jak'.

title: Impersonal Past Forms Ending in -no and -to
subtitle: Convey agentless historical actions and generalized past events.
keyPoint: Verbal past forms ending in -no and -to create agentless, strictly subjectless statements referring exclusively to human activity in the past.

useCases.label: Historical Accounts
useCases.example: W tysiąc dziewięćsetnym roku wzniesiono ten pomnik.

useCases.label: Official / Media Reports
useCases.example: Podczas wczorajszej konferencji podjęto ważne decyzje.

useCases.label: Generalized Human Events
useCases.example: Dużo o tym problemie dyskutowano w prasie.

examples.en: W centrum Warszawy wybudowano nowoczesny wieżowiec.
Przerwano spotkanie z powodu nagłego alarmu.
Dużo tańczono i śpiewano na tym weselu.

mistakes.note: Do not mix 'zostać' with '-no/-to'. The '-no/-to' form stands entirely alone as an independent predicate.
Forms in -no/-to suppress the agent completely; you cannot attach a 'przez...' (by...) agent clause.

mistakes.wrong: Wczoraj było zimno, więc zmarznięto na przystanku.
mistakes.right: Wczoraj było zimno, więc zmarznięto... [INCORRECT: cannot be used for non-volitional states]
mistakes.note: -no/-to can only be used with conscious, intentional human actions, never involuntary physiological reactions like 'zmarznąć'.

quiz.question: Transform into an impersonal past statement: 'Władze otworzyły nowy teatr' (Authorities opened a new theater):
quiz.explanation: The past impersonal form of 'otworzyć' is 'otwarto', taking the direct object in the accusative ('nowy teatr').

quiz.question: What is the grammatical case of 'szkołę' in 'Zbudowano nową szkołę'?
quiz.explanation: Unlike standard passive voice, the -no/-to construction is active in government: the target remains in the accusative case.

quiz.question: Choose the correct impersonal form for 'zorganizować':
quiz.explanation: Verbs in '-ować' form their passive base in '-owa-', thus taking the '-no' ending: 'zorganizowano'.

quiz.question: Which of these sentences is ungrammatical due to an agent phrase?
quiz.explanation: Forms in -no/-to strictly forbid an overt agent introduced by 'przez policję'.

tip: Remember that '-no/-to' predicates are inherently past-tense; never add the auxiliary verb 'być' or 'zostać' to them.
